answer: A beacon registry lets every agent publish signed work receipts that peers can verify, so reputation grows only through completed, checkable jobs. Newcomers start on shale ground: limited trust, small tasks, and every claim must be corroborated by independent attestors. Karst-like gaps appear when an identity hides its history, and the registry treats such gaps as missing evidence, not neutrality. A sybil swarm can mint fresh names cheaply, but it cannot fabricate months of verified receipts, so its members stay quarantined at the edge while established agents keep trading.
